title: No teachers, perfect pitch, and why she thinks studying is risky for jazz
summary: Her mother allowed no teachers; she later found she had perfect pitch. She argues that studying can destroy it and the feeling in a self-taught music like jazz, and says God steered her.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: At that early age did you have any professional teachers?

No, my mother wouldn't allow anyone to teach me because she took one lesson and after that she couldn't improvise any more. So she allowed no one to teach me and I'm very happy that she didn't because later on I discovered that I had a strong pitch, perfect pitch. In Pittsburgh I found out. I happened to be sitting in a class and the teacher had lost her harp. She couldn't give the class the tone to start their singing, so I told her I could do that, and she was surprised when I did it. She went out in the hall where the piano was and I had given her the right tone, and I discovered that I had perfect pitch.
Are there dangers in having perfect pitch or is it just a help?

It's a great help. It's a danger in studying early because you may lose it. I know some, great musicians that never lost it, like Dizzy Gillespie, but it's a danger in losing it through studying music, you know.
Why does studying make you lose it?

Well, because everything's on paper and you don't get any more sounds or anything. I think it's best, especially in jazz, for a musician to learn to feel everything and teach himself. If he's going to play the classics - like one summer I went to a teacher for about 2 weeks and I knew what to do, you see, but there's a danger in losing the feeling in jazz because it's a self-taught music and since I was going to play nothing but jazz I benefited by not studying...
How did you know you were going to play nothing but jazz?

Well, I never really knew but my guidance in life - I never really knew what I was going to do. I think God was working me towards doing greater things - I have a feeling about God using certain people to help others and they're - they really don't know what they're going to do but it works out that they're doing a terrific job for Him, and that has been my whole life. I never knew that I was going to play jazz or the classics but I knew that I loved jazz.
